unit.title: Рисуем классные вещи с помощью Turtle

learning_outcomes.statement: The learner can create a Turtle Screen/Turtle, move and turn it, and draw regular polygons using the 360/n exterior-angle formula.
The learner can use coordinates (goto), pen state (penup/pendown), color/fill, and seeded randomness together to build a small composed drawing (mandala, target).

criteria.rationale: No factual defects found; all Turtle behavior claims (heading convention, circle() direction, fill mechanics) verified against real rendered output via the chapter's Xvfb-based PNG pipeline.
Uses Python 3.14's standard-library turtle module throughout with no deprecated or version-sensitive API usage found.
'курс' (heading) correctly chosen over the false-friend calque 'заголовок' — the single highest-value terminology decision in this chapter; register entry added ([[heading-turtle-graphics]]).
The opener promises movement, turning, coordinates, pen/color/fill, randomness, debugging, and a mandala mini-project; all delivered with no gap.

All rendered-output claims are backed by the chapter's own real-execution pipeline (chapter_06_examples.py + Xvfb), independently confirmed passing via scripts/validate_chapter_06_outputs.py (33/33 examples).
Concrete, checkable scope (draw a square, a mandala, a target) rather than vague aspirations.
Assumes nothing beyond print()/import; every Turtle concept is new and introduced from scratch in dependency order (move -> turn -> repeat -> coordinates -> style -> randomness).
Frames Turtle as a visual, rewarding pivot after four text-only chapters — an effective motivational hook, not just a feature list.
18 sections chunked into clear sub-arcs (basic movement -> coordinates -> style -> randomness -> mini-projects) with two closing debugging/synthesis sections.
06-17 (debugging) and 06-18 (mini-projects) provide genuine consolidation; 06-19/06-20 additionally test retained understanding via browser-gradeable prediction exercises with no live window.
'курс' used identically and consistently across all 18 sections and into Chapter 7.
All internal cross-references and PAGES entries verified to resolve to real, populated sections.
The square/hexagon pattern discovered empirically in 06-04 is explicitly and correctly generalized (not silently repeated) into the 360/n formula in 06-11.
Chapter number, title, and all 18 section identifiers match the PAGES navigation model and sidebar exactly.
